models._models_note: Model artefacts are NOT committed or auto-downloaded. Extract one complete notebook-produced archive into a fresh directory, preserving bundle_manifest.json and nested paths. Startup verifies the selected graphs, all required sidecars/lineage, hashes, and serving contract; loose or mixed files are rejected.
models._frontier_note: The frontier (ViT-B/14, ~86M param) tier is OFF by default — it expects a GPU host we don't have. Set frontier_enabled=true AND extract its own complete manifest-bound bundle, including detector.onnx, under frontier_models_dir. When disabled OR if that bundle fails to load, /api/analyze?family=frontier returns available:false and /api/capabilities reports it unavailable. A bad frontier bundle never blocks gamma boot.

limits._fold_note: Classify the whole frame alongside the detected crops and fold it into the mean vote as one extra member (see MODEL_CARD.md). On by default — it is what recovers an over-cropped leaf shot. Turning it off saves one full ViT forward per scan and is the first latency lever to reach for, at the cost of that recovery.
limits._pro_quota_note: These process-local guest limits protect paid server work without forcing registration. Signed-in Free/PRO limits are authoritative in the account service; Aqua remains unlimited on-device.

ai._species_info_contact_note: A URL or e-mail put in the User-Agent of the species-info lookups (Wikipedia, Wikidata, Commons, iNaturalist). Wikimedia throttles anonymous clients first; blank still works.
ai._provider_note: Only an explicit test/development environment accepts openrouter_api_key. In production-like environments leave it blank and use an absolute owner-only openrouter_api_key_file; simultaneous/direct secrets fail closed. Comma-separated OpenRouter provider slugs this model may be routed to; blank lets OpenRouter route freely. Every request requires supported parameters, data_collection=deny, and a zero-data-retention endpoint. The configured model/provider/region and an aggregate cost ceiling remain release gates; see DEPLOYMENT.md and the PRO operations runbook.
ai._reasoning_note: gpt-5.6 treats effort as a CEILING, not a floor — an easy prompt may use no reasoning tokens even at 'high', so a higher setting costs nothing on the calls that don't need it. Levels: max/xhigh/high/medium/low/none ('minimal' is gpt-5.0-era and is mapped to 'low'), or 'omit' to send no reasoning field. Per-task overrides below win over this global default; medium is the floor because this content is factual and gets cached for days. Raising any of these means raising the matching *_max_tokens too — the hidden trace bills against max_tokens.
ai._prompt_caching_note: gpt-5.6 caches a prompt prefix only once it reaches 1024 tokens, charges 1.25x for the cache write and 0.1x for a cached read, and matches reliably only when the request carries a prompt_cache_key. Every system prompt this server sends therefore leads with one shared ~1400-token house preamble (ai_services._HOUSE_PREAMBLE), so the prefix clears the minimum on the first turn and one warm cache entry serves the chat doctor, both species screens and the care-plan polish alike. Keep prompt_cache_key identical across replicas that share a preamble — that is what routes them to the same warm machine; only give replicas distinct suffixes if one key becomes a hotspot under measured load. Watch /api/metrics -> prompt_cache.hit_ratio: a ratio near 0.0 over real traffic means the prefix changed or fell under the minimum.

plantnet._plantnet_secret_note: Only an explicit test/development environment accepts plantnet_api_key. In production-like environments leave it blank and mount an absolute owner-only plantnet_api_key_file. Unsafe files and simultaneous direct/file values disable PlantNet before any upstream call. Every uncached network attempt also requires the shared account-service budget authority.

security._community_author_key_pepper_note: Stable server-side transform for account-free Community author credentials at rest. Set the same value on every replica and do not rotate it without a key-migration plan; changing it makes existing device handles unreachable. It is intentionally independent from the rotatable IP privacy pepper.
security._feedback_ip_pepper_note: Secret used to pepper the SHA-256 of a client IP before it is stored (feedback / community / telemetry client_ip_hash). IPv4 is only a 32-bit space, so a hash with a known or empty pepper enumerates back to the raw IP in seconds — it MUST be a high-entropy per-deployment secret. Leave blank and the server generates one on first use and persists it beside the feedback DB as .ip_hash_pepper; set it explicitly to control rotation or to share one pepper across replicas.
security._training_note: De-identified model-improvement capture requires both this operator switch and the current per-request consent disclosure version. Only detector-backed leaf crops are retained; no full-frame fallback, user/account/install/scan identifier, IP/hash, filename, URL, or free text enters training.db. Export/review is offline only through tools/export_training_data.py.

push._fcm_note: Path to a Firebase service-account JSON for FCM HTTP v1 push (opinion notifications). Empty => push is a no-op. Keep this file OUT of git. The Android FCM *client* values (FCM_APP_ID / API_KEY / PROJECT_ID / SENDER_ID) are NOT server config — they live in the app build (see DEPLOYMENT.md).
